purpose: Archival evidence for territory reading pages. Images are historical source material, not generated decoration.
notes: Image rights statements are recorded from each linked Commons description page. Source pages give the detailed jurisdictional basis.
Downloaded at appropriate web resolution with no AI editing, recolouring or synthetic reconstruction.
Captions separate visible evidence, collection descriptions and interpretation.

images.alt: Gandhi bends to pick up salt while other participants watch.
images.caption: Gandhi at Dandi during the Salt March, April 1930. Making salt challenged the colonial salt monopoly; the photograph captures an act of civil disobedience.
images.provenanceNote: Source filename gives 5 April, while accounts of the salt-law breach commonly date it 6 April. Caption deliberately gives month only. Downloaded Commons thumbnail; no editing.

images.alt: A group of workers stand and cut sugar cane in a Jamaican field.
images.caption: Cane cutters in Jamaica, 1891. This photograph was taken decades after emancipation. It shows plantation work continuing, not people who can be identified as enslaved.
images.credit: Valentine & Sons / The Caribbean Photo Archive, via Wikimedia Commons
images.provenanceNote: Do not caption these people as enslaved: photograph dates to 1891. Downloaded Commons thumbnail; no editing.

images.alt: Dock workers pull a loaded cart beside sailing ships in Hong Kong.
images.caption: Dock workers in Hong Kong, catalogued as 1890. The image brings human labour into a history often told through ports, treaties and trade totals.
images.provenanceNote: Commons record dates photograph 1890; creator not identified. Original600px file retained without upscaling or editing.

images.alt: Delegates pose on the steps of Government House during the Charlottetown Conference.
images.caption: Delegates at the Charlottetown Conference, September 1864. The meeting helped prepare Confederation. Consider whose participation this formal group portrait records—and whose voice it leaves outside the frame.
images.credit: George P. Roberts / Library and Archives Canada, C-000733, via Wikimedia Commons
images.provenanceNote: Commons sourced to Library and Archives Canada MIKAN3623696. Downloaded Commons thumbnail; no editing.

images.alt: A crowd and uniformed troops gather outside the decorated Treasury building in Brisbane.
images.caption: Federation Day in Brisbane, 1901. Lord Lamington reads the proclamation from the Treasury building as a crowd gathers below. Flags and ceremony connect the new Commonwealth with the Empire.
images.credit: H. W. Mobsby / John Oxley Library, State Library of Queensland, image 139704, via Wikimedia Commons
images.provenanceNote: Original765×1000file downloaded; no editing. Keep complete portrait composition where possible.

images.alt: Passengers and workers stand beside a steam train and the station building in Nairobi.
images.caption: Nairobi station on the Uganda Railway, about the 1900s. The postcard records infrastructure and everyday activity, but cannot by itself explain who benefited or how the railway was built.
images.credit: D. V. Figueira, Mombasa (postcard publisher; photographer unidentified), via Wikimedia Commons
images.provenanceNote: Publisher visible on postcard. Commons gives approximate1900s date and unknown photographer. Original940×601file downloaded; no editing.
